content.text:
Looking at the data:

- F3Z01 has only 3 streams: Zone temp sensor, heating setpoint, cooling setpoint.
- Setpoints are constant (~26.7 C cool, ~15.6-21 C heat) throughout.
- F3Z01 temp is ~24-25 C year-round, mildly rising (Jan 23.9 → Dec 25.0).
- The other zones' temp sensors (F3Z02, F3Z03, F3Z05, F4Z01, etc.) follow a normal seasonal pattern: ~21-22 C in winter, peak ~25 C in summer, back down to ~22 C in winter.
- F3Z01 does not follow the seasonal dip: in Dec it is 25.0 vs F3Z02 22.3, F3Z05 23.3, F4Z01 23.1.

So F3Z01 is persistently higher. To discriminate between "local load change" and "zone sensor fault" we would need an independent signal that reflects real load (or real temperature) of F3Z01 — e.g., the zone's electric power draw, occupancy, CO2, or the controller's output/valve flow — none of which is in the catalog for F3Z01. Power (95a195d5-…), CO2 (f7b2e083-…) exist in the graph as points but have no timeseries. With only the single temperature stream plus constant setpoints, both hypotheses ("F3Z01 genuinely warmer due to load" and "F3Z01 sensor drifted upward") fit the available data equally well.
